newsitem.title: GERMANY: Consumer resistance seen weighing on German wheat.
newsitem.headline: Consumer resistance seen weighing on German wheat.

text.p: German wheat markets are quietly steady but a lack of consumer buying interest is expected to weigh on prices, brokers said.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week kept its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) at 280 marks a tonne and maintained spot feed wheat free Hamburg at 275.
Feed wheat demand was high and transport surcharges during the cold spell earlier this month had temporarily buoyed prices, but this strength had failed to spill over into bread wheat.
Warmer weather looked set to free up transport, and barge shipments to compound feed plants might resume soon.
Export brokers also feared German material might not feature heavily in any EU export allocations at Thursday's weekly tender.
Last week, German wheat accounted for only 1,000 tonnes of the 260,000 given subsidies.
Eastern European export prospects steadied prices as Mecklenburg state traders reported some sales to Poland.
Uzbek business was also expected for February/March.
In the fob Baltic export market, brokers put normal spot bread wheat (12 percent protein) for second half January at a little changed 286-287.50 marks this week.
They kept higher quality offers steady on the week at around 292-308, depending on protein levels.
Fob Baltic barley was quoted 2.50-3.00 marks higher at 257.50-274 marks, boosted by expectations of a large EU barley inclusion in Saudi Feb/March purchases of 1.2 million tonnes.
Fob rye offers were up 1.50-3.00 marks at 254-268 after domestic millers bought bread rye.
